title: Seesaw Split

examples.explanation: Put the pivot under position 2: 2 + 7 = 9 on the left and 3 + 6 = 9 on the right.
No position balances the two sides.

approaches.name: total sum and a running left sum
sum both sides at every position

steps.title: Clarify the input
steps.description: Asks what to return when several positions balance or none do, and whether weights can be negative.
look_for: asks which position to return if several work
hints: Before you start, is there anything about the answer you'd want to pin down?
If two different positions both balance, which one should you give back?
Settle which position wins, the no-answer case and negative weights first.

steps.title: Avoid re-adding both sides
steps.description: Uses the total sum and a running left sum so each position is checked in constant time.
look_for: right side is total minus left minus current
hints: Look at how much adding up your code does at each position.
If you know the total and the left side, do you need to add up the right side?
Keep a running left sum; the right side is the total minus the left minus the current weight.

steps.title: Exclude the pivot itself
steps.description: Doesn't count the weight at the pivot on either side.
look_for: subtracts the current weight from the right side
updates the left sum after the check
hints: Check which side the weight at the pivot ends up on in your code.
Should the weight sitting on the pivot count toward the left, the right, or neither?
The pivot weight belongs to neither side; compare before adding it to the left sum.

steps.title: Return the first match or -1
steps.description: Stops at the leftmost balancing position and gives -1 if there isn't one.
hints: Try your code on a list where nothing balances.
What does your function give back if the loop finds nothing?
Stop at the first balancing position; if there isn't one, the answer is -1.

common_mistakes.description: includes the pivot weight in the left or right sum
recomputes both sums at every position
common_mistakes.symptom: correct but O(n^2) on long lists

common_mistakes.description: assumes weights are positive and stops early
common_mistakes.symptom: fails lists with negative weights like [3, -3, 9]

wrap_up_questions: What are the time and space complexity?
How would you find a split into two halves with equal sums, where every weight goes to one side?

origin_note: Original. Pattern: total sum and a running left sum.
